speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. Additionally, have you noticed any sudden changes in your vision, such as blurriness, loss of peripheral vision, or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. As a 69-year-old woman, could you specify if your vision is worsening in one eye or both, and does the headache have a specific location like the front, side, or back of your head? Also, have you noticed any halos around lights, headaches upon waking, or any neurological deficits like weakness or numbness?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain_With_Contrast: No contrast-enhancing lesions, mass effect, or signs of acute intracranial hemorrhage identified; no specific abnormalities detected in the requested scan data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI has ruled out tumors, hemorrhage, or acute structural lesions. Since your vision is worsening progressively over three weeks, have you noticed any specific visual field defects, such as a "curtain" coming down over your vision, or any floaters/flashes? Also, does the headache worsen when you bend over or strain, and have you had any recent trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI has effectively ruled out primary brain tumors and acute hemorrhage. Given your progressive vision changes and headache, I need to know if you are experiencing transient episodes of vision loss (amaurosis fugax) or if you notice any jaw pain when chewing, which could suggest Giant Cell Arteritis. Additionally, have you noticed any new onset of floaters or flashes of light, and does the headache feel like a severe pressure behind one eye?

REQUEST TEST: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate)
REQUEST TEST: CRP (C-Reactive Protein)
REQUEST TEST: Visual_Field_Test

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ESR: 45 mm/hr; CRP: 2.8 mg/dL; Visual_Field_Test: Significant constriction of peripheral vision with a central scotoma noted in both eyes, consistent with the worsening vision reported.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ESR of 45 and elevated CRP, combined with the MRI ruling out structural lesions, strongly suggest an inflammatory cause for your headaches and vision loss. Before we conclude, are you experiencing any jaw pain when chewing, scalp tenderness, or any difficulty swallowing?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis
